sections.section_name: Section A - Multiple Choice Questions (MCQs) / Fill in the Blanks

questions.question_text: In Scratch programming, which type of block is primarily used to make a character (sprite) move across the screen?
Fill in the blank: In a school museum, a written description placed next to an exhibited artifact explaining its history is called a __________.
Which of the following recipes is considered a safe 'Cooking Without Fire' activity?
options: B) Making a fresh fruit salad
D) Baking a cake in an oven
questions.answer: B) Making a fresh fruit salad

questions.question_text: What is the background image on the Scratch screen where all the sprites perform their actions called?
Fill in the blank: Before starting any fireless cooking activity, it is strictly mandatory to wash your ________ thoroughly with soap.

sections.section_name: Section B - Very Short Answer (VSA) / Definitions

questions.question_text: Explain the role of a 'Curator' when organizing a school or class museum. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: A curator is responsible for selecting, organizing, and safely displaying historical or artistic items in the museum while ensuring each artifact has an accurate informational label.

questions.question_text: What is the primary benefit of learning 'Cooking Without Fire' for middle school students? [20-30 words]
questions.answer: It teaches students basic culinary independence, safe food handling, and nutrition awareness without exposing them to the physical dangers of open gas flames or hot oil.

questions.question_text: In Scratch animation, what is a 'Sprite' and how can a user change its appearance? [20-30 words]
questions.answer: A sprite is a digital character or object in Scratch. Users can easily change its appearance by modifying its 'Costumes' using the built-in paint editor.

questions.question_text: You are assigned to create a simple interactive game in Scratch where a cat chases a mouse. Describe the basic logical steps or blocks you would use to program the mouse to move away randomly when the cat gets near. [35-45 words]
questions.answer: I would use a 'Forever' loop containing an 'If...Then' control block. Inside, I would add a 'Touching [Cat]' sensing block. If the condition is true, I would command the mouse to 'Glide' to a 'Random Position' or use a 'Move [10] Steps' motion block away.
